title: Pauri 24, meaning: no end to praise
hook: there is no end to His praise, His works, His gifts; the more is said, the more remains (Japji 24)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sound of Pauri 24. Your line was ant na siftee: end at both ends, and no end in the middle. Today, what the whole stanza says. Day two hundred two.

You know that feeling when you try to thank someone who really changed your life. A teacher, a grandparent, the friend who got you through the worst year. You say thank you. Then you remember something else they did. Then something else. You write a card, and the card's too small. The more you say, the more there is to say. That isn't a failure of your words. It's a sign of how much there was. Pauri 24 is built on exactly that feeling.
screen: `THANKING SOMEONE WHO CHANGED YOU.` → `ONE MORE THING, ONE MORE.` → `THE CARD IS TOO SMALL.`

segments.voice: Pauri 24 is a long chain of the word ant, end. In paraphrase: no end to the praises, no end to telling them. No end to His works, no end to His giving. No end to seeing, no end to hearing. His mind's purpose can't be known to its end. The created world can't be known to its end, nor its near shore, nor its far one. So many cry out wanting to find its limits, and its limits can't be found. No one knows this end. And then the line behind today's carry, in the original: bahutaa aakheeai bahutaa hoe. The more is said, the more there is. Think about how strange that is. Usually saying things uses them up. You tell a story and it's told. Here it's the opposite. Every word of praise opens more to praise. Then the stanza climbs, in paraphrase: great is the Master, high His place, and higher than high is His Name. Only someone as high as He could know Him. Only He knows how great He is. And the last line: Nanak, the gift comes by the glance of grace. That's the stanza's quiet resting point. We can't reach the end by talking. What we have comes as a gift, through nadar, grace, a word we'll keep meeting in Japji. So the praising never finishes, and that's not a problem to fix. It's what praising something infinite feels like from inside. Like the card that's too small, it tells you how much there was.
screen: `NO END TO WORKS, GIFTS, SEEING.` · `BAHUTAA AAKHEEAI BAHUTAA HOE.` · `HIGHER THAN HIGH, HIS NAME.` · `THE GIFT COMES BY GRACE.` · then, large: `THE MORE REMAINS.`

segments.voice: Pick one thing, a person, a place, the morning light, and praise it silently for one full minute without stopping. When you think you've run out, keep going: find one more thing to notice about it, and one more. See whether the more you say, the more there is. Then let the words stop and sit with what's left over. The bell holds the time.
Pauri 24. No end to the praises, the works, the gifts; the more is said, the more there is; and the gift comes by grace.
Your line: the more remains. Today, thank one person for one thing, then add one more thing, and notice there's still more. Day two hundred two.

howItsDone: Pauri 24 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; Sikhs often quote bahutaa aakheeai bahutaa hoe to say that praise of the One never runs out.

original.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 24: the more is said, the more there is.

trapdoor: what you thought: God is very big.
what it means: praise never finishes, because every word of it opens more; the gift comes by grace.
what a scholar hears: the stanza repeats ant, end, in almost every line; its close, nadaree karmee daat, ties the endless to nadar, grace.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 5 (Japji, Pauri 24, the rest of the stanza)
